Question: When you go to a barber shop, can you get a haircut and get your hair dyed at the same time?
Answer: You can, provided your Barber does color. Some states have what is known as a restricted barbers license. Barbara's carrying a restricted license are not covered to perform chemical services. Cosmetologist can do it all. A suggestion, instead of getting a permanent hair color go for a demi-permanent. This will grow out with less of a line of demarcation. If you wear your hair short, by the time you get ready for your next haircut it'll be time to do the color again. It's best to go a level or two lighter than your natural color, and blend your Grays rather than cover them. If you are covering gray hair. If you're just making your hair a different color you can go the same level or darker with a demi permanent but you cannot go lighter.

Question: Should I go back to the salon to ask for a fix if my color correction is fading within a few washes? My hair was botched, bleached white, fried. I had lowlights and toner added to hide the blotchy spots but now the color is awful.
Answer: The type of fading you are experiencing is 100% predictable. Anytime your hair is highly compromised the way your hair is, it's impossible to have the hair hang on to color for long. Normally we suggest using a color enhancing shampoo to keep the color rich and help to counteract some of the fading. But when you have highlights and lowlights combined, a color enhancing shampoo is kind of hard to use because you can either use one to keep the brown lowlights rich, this will affect the blonde pieces. It will make them darker. Or, you use a color enhancing shampoo to add tone back to your blonde highlights, this would be too light to address the low light fading. You should have been sent home with a no sulfate shampoo and conditioner to help you maintain the color. You cannot be shampooing everyday, you cannot be getting your hair wet with salt water or chlorine. The more heat you put on your hair the more fading you are going to have in addition to your already compromised hair. You can go back to the salon and talk to the colorist and see if there's anything he or she can suggest. Sometimes it can take several applications. Non - Ammonia color will hang on to the hair longer due to the compromise state that it's in. But since I don't know what the color is used I cannot predict anything nor can anyone else on this forum. I always teach in my color correction classes the importance of educating the client about how quickly high lift blonde Corrections going darker, will fade. It's not a one-time fix. All the technology we have available to us, you can't put hair back where there isn't any. Meaning if the hair shaft is compromised from continual abuse from application of chemical services, we can't put fiber back into the hair. It must be amputated and grown back out.

Question: What are the best chemical and natural ingredients in an anti-dandruff shampoo?
Answer: Look for shampoos containing pyrithione zinc, selenium sulfide or tea tree oil. Make sure you really have dandruff and not dry flaky scalp. The two are completely different conditions. Dry flaky scalp will be accompanied by small dry Flakes and an itchy scalp. Dandruff will be accompanied by largest yellowish colored flakes that are oily. Oftentimes they will peel away from the scalp in pieces as small as your pinky fingernail or as large as a quarter. If you have dry itchy scalp, look for moisturizing shampoos and conditioners instead.

Question: What does a LICE check at school detect? Does it only look for nits and larvae, or can it also detect adult live head lice?
Answer: They will be looking for all three. But the easiest to spot are the nits because they are little white particles that attach to the hair shaft. Lice on the scalp depending on the color of lice and the scalp may not be as easy to see. And they can move too. As well as larvae they move also. Lice can range in color from a pale tan to darker brown.
